name: March 18, 2025 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MARCH 18, 2025
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Skophammer called the meeting to order at 6:31 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dane Skophammer, Vice Chair Alicia Peak, Commissioners Georgia
  Goldfarb (arrived at 6:39 p.m.), Jake Lingo, and Judy Villablanca

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; and Brittany Saleaumua,
  Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Skophammer led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Vice Chair Peak moved, and Commissioner Villablanca seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0;
  Commissioner Goldfarb absent (arrived at 6:39 p.m.).

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on March 13, 2025.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A. Administration of Oath to Newly Appointed Commissioners

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua administered the Oath of Office to Chair
  Skophammer and Commissioner Villablanca.

  B. Election of Chair and Vice Chair

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  all flve Commissioners must be present to hold elections. She stated the item
  would be continued to the April 15, 2025 Regular meeting.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Joe Sichta reiterated his request to contract with Class Aquatics. The organization
  would share pool time with the Malibu Marlins at the Malibu Community Pool. He
  stated that Councilmember Silverstein had supported sharing pool time between
  two organizations. He requested that the Commission review the rules of three
  swimmers per lane. He stated that private funding was secured by Class Aquatics
  and the Malibu Aquatics Foundation.

  Chair Skophammer and Vice Chair Peak thanked Mr. Sichta for his time.

  Commissioner Goldfarb arrived at 6:39 p.m.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Lingo moved, and Vice Chair Peak seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  l.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the November l9, 2024
  Parks and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in November 2024, December 2024, January 2025, and February 2025.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Jake Kurediian Citizenship Award

  Recommended Action: Discuss the nomination process for the 2025 Jake Kuredjian
  Citizenship Award.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Chair Skophammer stated that Julia Holland was involved in multiple art—related
  programs and served on the Malibu Arts Commission for several years. He stated
   Parks and Recraation Commission

  that Suzanne Guldimann would be a good candidate due to her environmental work
  and years of service on the Parks and Recreation Commission.

  Commissioner Goldfarb indicated agreement with Chair Skophammer.

  Commissioner Lingo suggested opening the public nomination period to acquire
  public feedback and the Commission would discuss potential recipients after the
  nomination period was closed.

  Chair Skophammer agreed with Commissioner Lingo and stated he wanted to
  nominate John Mills. He stated Mr. Mills was instrumental in the youth football
  program and was involved in various sports programs.

  Vice Chair Peak stated she wanted to nominate Heather Gardner for her
  involvement with the Skate Park and middle school sports. She also stated that Nick
  Shurgot should be considered, due to his involvement with Malibu Little League
  and American Youth Soccer Organization (AYSO).

  Commissioner Lingo indicated agreement with Vice Chair Peak regarding the
  nomination ofNick Shurgot. He stated Mr. Shurgot was instrumental to the success
  of Malibu Little League during the Pandemic.

CONSENSUS
  By Consensus, the Commission agreed to open the public nomination period for
  the 2025 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award.

  B.  Naming Rights Policy and Permanent Skate Park

  Recommended Action: l) Receive and flle City Council Policy #52 Naming Rights
  for Public Facilities; and 2) Provide feedback regarding community donation
  outreach for the Permanent Skate Park.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated City facilities should not be named after commercial
  entities.

  Chair Skophammer stated the Commission would review a list of names and advise
  the City Council on which names to consider.

  Commissioner Villablanca stated that the policy did not encourage commercial
  entities to apply for naming rights but it did not exclude them. She believed
  residents would be interested in supporting the project financially.

  In response to Commissioner Villablanca, Vice Chair Peak stated that the Landon
  family paid for the Michael Landon Center to be built and requested that the
  building be named after Michael Landon.

  Chair Skophammer stated that there could potentially be Malibu residents that
  would pay to have their name on a facility, and the Naming Rights Policy was a
  step in the right direction to get facilities built in Malibu.

  Commissioner Goldfarb recommended installing plaques at the Skate Park for
  those who have donated to the project.

  Vice Chair Peak stated the Schaar Family would be interested in providing a
  donation.

  Community Services Director Riesgo stated the City Council did not provide
  specific thresholds. She stated that Council wanted the park to be named Malibu
  Skate Park.

  In response to Commissioner Villablanca, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the approved budget for the Permanent Skatepark proj ect was $5.1 Million.

  Commissioner Lingo stated the City should create a pamphlet that lists the naming
  rights criteria and amenities to promote fundraising opportunities.

  Chair Skophammer stated the Commission should aim to find a donor to provide
  funding for the entire cost of the Skate Park.

  The Commission discussed the Skate Park amenities that could be named and
  where a potential plaque wall could be installed.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on the Recreation Guide,
  registration software, Marlins Swim Team, Senior programs, Dial-A-Ride,
  Equestrian Park, Charmlee Night Hike, Scout Program, Bluffs Chronolog, Trancas
  Field, Pony Field Conversion, Trail Maintenance, Raptor Posts, Permanent Skate
  Park, Community Lands, and April Commission meeting.

  Commissioner Lingo stated he would not attend the April 15, 2025 Regular
  meeting.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Chair Skophammer stated that the Public
  Safety Commission would be better suited to review options for a lecture on fire
  ecology, restoration, and plant regrowth.

  Commissioner Villablanca stated she was looking forward to serving on the
  Commission.

  Vice Chair Peak stated the city made a poor choice to cancel the Youth Basketball
  League following the Palisades Fire. She also suggested rescheduling Commission
  meetings when possible, rather than canceling since the Commission met once a
  month.

  Commissioner Lingo stated the Malibu Little League Opening Day was a success
  and thanked Recreation Supervisor Orosz for his help to ensure the park was ready
  for League games and practices.

  In response to Commissioner Lingo, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  the Commission would be involved in the public outreach process for the Malibu
  Bluffs Park Snack Shack project.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Skophammer adjourned the meeting at 8:31 p.m.
